title: Apply language-neutral secure coding foundations: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: For untrusted API/web data, which control decides whether input is acceptable, how it is stored/interpreted, who may act on it, and how it is safely returned?
focalInsight: Input validation, output encoding, error handling, authentication, authorization, API object access, and secret protection.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Secure Coding
nodes.definition: Repeatable coding and review practices that prevent or reduce known weakness classes while preserving intended behavior under normal, invalid, and hostile conditions.
nodes.decision: Apply language/architecture-aware standards, threat-informed review, tests, exception governance, and production feedback.
nodes.failureExample: A one-time secure-coding course without review and testing does not control a new authorization defect.
nodes.detail: Repeatable coding and review practices that prevent or reduce known weakness classes while preserving intended behavior under normal, invalid, and hostile conditions.

nodes.label: Input Validation
nodes.definition: Server-side enforcement that untrusted data has permitted type, structure, length, range, encoding, and business meaning before use.
nodes.decision: Validate syntactic and semantic rules as close as practical to receipt; allowlist expected values and treat client validation as UX, not security.
nodes.failureExample: A client-side-only price check can be bypassed by a crafted request.
nodes.detail: Server-side enforcement that untrusted data has permitted type, structure, length, range, encoding, and business meaning before use.

nodes.label: Output Encoding
nodes.definition: Transforming data for the exact output interpreter/context so untrusted content is displayed as data rather than executed as markup, script, URL, or other code.
nodes.decision: Encode when emitting data into its target context and use suitable rendering APIs; do not rely on input filters to predict future contexts.
nodes.failureExample: HTML encoding text placed inside a JavaScript context can still create executable behavior.
nodes.detail: Transforming data for the exact output interpreter/context so untrusted content is displayed as data rather than executed as markup, script, URL, or other code.

nodes.label: Error Handling
nodes.definition: Safe handling of expected and unexpected failures that preserves availability and diagnosability without exposing internal details or secrets.
nodes.decision: Return minimal user-facing errors, log protected diagnostic context, and define safe rollback/failure behavior.
nodes.failureExample: An API stack trace can disclose schema, paths, or tokens that help an attacker.
nodes.detail: Safe handling of expected and unexpected failures that preserves availability and diagnosability without exposing internal details or secrets.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.definition: Verification of the identity or credential presented by a user, service, or device.
nodes.decision: Choose strong, managed authentication appropriate to the actor and protect credential/token lifecycle; authentication alone does not grant object access.
nodes.failureExample: A valid customer token may still be used to request another customer’s invoice.
nodes.detail: Verification of the identity or credential presented by a user, service, or device.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.definition: Enforcement of whether an authenticated principal may perform a requested action on a specific object or resource in the current context.
nodes.decision: Check server-side at each sensitive action/object boundary using least privilege and deny-by-default behavior.
nodes.failureExample: Checking only that a token is valid enables insecure direct object access.
nodes.detail: Enforcement of whether an authenticated principal may perform a requested action on a specific object or resource in the current context.

nodes.label: API Security
nodes.definition: Protection of programmatic interfaces through identity, object/action authorization, input/schema validation, rate/replay controls, data minimization, versioning, safe errors, and observability.
nodes.decision: Model API abuse paths and test valid/invalid callers, object IDs, token reuse, rate behavior, and response data.
nodes.failureExample: An authenticated API with no object-level authorization can expose every tenant’s data.
nodes.detail: Protection of programmatic interfaces through identity, object/action authorization, input/schema validation, rate/replay controls, data minimization, versioning, safe errors, and observability.

nodes.label: Secrets
nodes.definition: Credentials, keys, tokens, connection strings, and sensitive values whose disclosure or misuse grants access or weakens controls.
nodes.decision: Use managed scoped storage/retrieval, rotation, revocation, redaction, and separate environment identities; never hardcode or expose them in errors/logs.
nodes.failureExample: A database password embedded in client code can be extracted and used outside the intended application.
nodes.detail: Credentials, keys, tokens, connection strings, and sensitive values whose disclosure or misuse grants access or weakens controls.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: For untrusted API/web data, which control decides whether input is acceptable, how it is stored/interpreted, who may act on it, and how it is safely returned?
learningContract.misconception: Input allowlisting alone prevents injection/XSS, and authentication proves access to every object.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: Input validation, output encoding, error handling, authentication, authorization, API object access, and secret protection.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Do not prescribe one schema language, query API, authentication protocol, encoding library, or secret manager.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: A partner submits a comment that will be stored and later rendered to a finance dashboard. State the validation, authorization, query, encoding, error, and logging decisions.
